papers.title: LMPPNet: a lightweight multi-scale physical prior network for single image dehazing
papers.abstract: In recent years, while the performance of deep learning-based image dehazing technology has been continuously advancing, it inevitably incurs an increase in computational overhead. To strike a favorable balance between performance and computational cost, this paper proposes a novel lightweight single image dehazing network. The network comprises two core modules: (1) the Efficient Depthwise Adaptive Fusion Module (EDAFM) integrates multiscale learning strategies with depthwise convolutions to enable efficient extraction of haze features; (2) the Physical Prior Reconstruction Module (PPRM) leverages the Atmospheric Scattering Model to realize high-quality clear image reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed network achieves competitive dehazing performance, even with remarkably few parameters. The code is available at https://github.com/wddfds/LMPPNet.

papers.title: Single Image Dehazing Using Fuzzy Region Segmentation and Haze Density Decomposition
papers.abstract: Images captured under haze weather conditions usually suffer from visual quality degradations, such as blurred details, faded colors, and decreased saturation. Existing physics-based dehazing methods mainly have two drawbacks: 1) the atmospheric light is treated as a constant for the entire image, and 2) pixel- or patch-based strategies are employed to estimate the model parameters, resulting in inaccurate haze density estimations. Therefore, these methods may lead to over-dehazing or under-dehazing due to insufficient utilization of features from regions with similar haze densities. To address these issues, a novel single image dehazing framework based on fuzzy region segmentation and haze density decomposition is proposed. Specifically, a region-based physical model that considers the non-uniform atmospheric light is first constructed based on the classic atmospheric scattering model. Then, a fuzzy segmentation algorithm is improved to divide the input hazy image into several separate regions. Subsequently, we formulate a simple linear relationship between the atmospheric light and brightness to estimate region-based atmospheric light. On the other hand, we develop a novel haze density decomposition algorithm based on boundary constraints to separate the atmospheric veil into two components: thin part and dense part. Three haze-related features, contrast, gradient and clarity, are extracted from the input hazy image to construct weight maps and a multi-scale fusion is further exploited to combine weight maps and boundary veils to acquire the refined atmospheric veil. Finally, the model inversion is performed to acquire the haze-free result. Experiments on six diverse hazy datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms several state-of-the-art dehazing methods in both visual quality and objective evaluation.

papers.title: A differentiable multi-physics learning model for robust single-image dehazing under complex atmospheric conditions
papers.abstract: Restoring clear visibility from a single hazy image remains a challenging inverse problem when multiple atmospheric phenomena jointly affect image formation. In real environments, light propagation can be influenced not only by particle scattering but also by turbulence-induced blur and wavelength-dependent attenuation. Most existing dehazing approaches primarily address scattering, which limits their physical consistency and robustness in heavy haze or long-range scenes. In this work, we introduce a differentiable multi-physics learning framework that is designed to integrate scattering, turbulence, and spectral attenuation within a unified image formation model. The degradation process is expressed as a compact linear observation equation, where turbulence is represented through a spatial convolution operator and spectral effects are modeled via channel-dependent attenuation. Since the governing parameters cannot be directly inferred from a single observation, the formulated as an iterative refinement process guided by a learned approximation of the physical model. A lightweight neural estimator predicts the observation operators, while a learnable spectral module captures wavelength-dependent behavior. An iterative regularization network stabilizes the reconstruction process and prevents error propagation. Experiments conducted on the RESIDE-SOTS benchmark show competitive performance, achieving PSNR/SSIM values of 27.3/0.94 for indoor scenes and 30.2/0.94 for outdoor scenes with only a few optimization steps. Additional analyses confirm improved robustness under noise perturbations and severe illumination variations, highlighting the effectiveness of differentiable learning with physics-inspired constraints for real-world atmospheric image restoration.

papers.title: SpectraMixNet: lightweight multi-scale spectral-frequency attention network for single image dehazing
A Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network Based On The Atmospheric Scattering Model For Real-Time Video Dehazing
papers.abstract: Videos captured in outdoor environments are often degraded by atmospheric scattering and the attenuation of reflected light caused by suspended particles, which reduce image contrast and visibility. Under severe haze conditions, the visual quality of the captured scenes becomes significantly blurred and unclear. Most recent dehazing methods primarily rely on convolutional neural networks and are designed for single-image restoration. However, when individually dehazed frames are played continuously as a video, shadow-like artifacts and temporal inconsistencies may appear, resulting in unsatisfactory visual performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a fast single-image dehazing model based on a lightweight deep learning network and a reformulated atmospheric scattering model. Specifically, features are extracted separately from the three channels of the RGB color space to jointly estimate the medium transmission map and atmospheric light parameters. Although the proposed model is originally designed for single-image dehazing, it can be applied to videos in a frame-wise manner due to its low computational complexity. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves competitive dehazing performance while maintaining high inference speed, and it demonstrates promising generalization ability in real-world hazy scenes without significant degradation in visual quality. In addition, video quality evaluations indicate that the frame-wise application of the proposed model can still produce favorable perceptual video quality, making it a practical solution for real-time image and video dehazing applications.

papers.title: An improved MixDehazeNet for image dehazing via cross-scale interaction and structure-aware convolution
papers.abstract: To enhance the imaging quality and target recognition capability of polarized images under low-altitude adverse weather conditions, this paper proposes an improved dehazing network for polarized images based on the original MixDehazeNet architecture. The proposed network incorporates a Lightweight Cross-Scale Module (LCSM) and an Efficient Structure- Aware Convolution (ESAC) module. Built upon the U-Net framework, the network leverages the inherent advantages of polarization imaging in scattering suppression and contrast enhancement, while optimizing its architecture for highresolution image processing. The ESAC module adopts a mixture-of-experts mechanism to adaptively model diverse structural features, whereas the LCSM module enables efficient interaction and fusion of multi-scale features. The proposed model contains as few as 4.4 million parameters, offering excellent deployment efficiency and application potential. Compared with existing dehazing networks such as Focal-Net and MixDehazeNet, the proposed approach achieves more effective haze removal and significantly alleviates issues such as detail loss.

papers.title: SensaNet: A Lightweight DL Model for Tuberculosis Detection in Histopathological Images
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis remains a global health problem, particularly in resource-limited settings in which early and accurate diagnosis is paramount. This research presents SensaNet, an efficient yet light-weight binary tuberculosis (TB) classification for histopathological image patches. SensaNet is evaluated against a well-curated set of 27,987 Kinyoun-stained image patches that were scanned from digitized slides of sputum smears, with wellbalanced bacilli-positive and negative distributions. SensaNet combines current architectural innovations such as Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks, Swish activation, and single-head self-attention to amplify feature representation in channel and spatial domains with lower memory cost. Experimental results confirm that SensaNet achieves an accuracy of 98.54%, precision of 98.19%, and recall of 98.95%, outperforming several baseline architectures on sensitivity with the compact size of 12.2 MB and only above 1 million parameters. Comparative analysis proves SensaNet's suitability for TB diagnosis, offering a good trade-off between diagnostic performance and computational expense. These results weigh in favor of the model's potential deployment for real-time point-of-care diagnostics, particularly for low-resource environments.

papers.title: GUSL-Dehaze: A Green U-Shaped Learning Approach to Image Dehazing
papers.abstract: Image dehazing is a restoration task that aims to recover a clear image from a single hazy input. Traditional approaches rely on statistical priors and the physics-based atmospheric scattering model to reconstruct the haze-free image. While recent state-of-the-art methods are predominantly based on deep learning architectures, these models often involve high computational costs and large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for resource-constrained devices. In this work, we propose GUSL-Dehaze, a Green U-Shaped Learning approach to image dehazing. Our method integrates a physics-based model with a green learning (G L) framework, offering a lightweight, transparent alternative to conventional deep learning techniques. Unlike neural network-based solutions, GUSL-Dehaze completely avoids deep learning. Instead, we begin with an initial dehazing step using a modified Dark Channel Prior (DCP), which is followed by a green learning pipeline implemented through a U -shaped architecture. This architecture employs unsupervised representation learning for effective feature extraction, together with feature-engineering techniques such as Relevant Feature Test (RFT) [1] and Least-Squares Normal Transform (LNT) [2] to maintain a compact model size. Finally, the dehazed image is obtained via a transparent supervised learning strategy. G USL-Dehaze significantly reduces parameter count while ensuring mathematical interpretability and achieving performance on par with state-of-the-art deep learning models.

papers.title: MHAze-Net: a multi-head residual unet with attention-guided fusion-discriminator for single-image dehazing
Stability-Aware Physics-Prior Conditioning for Lightweight Image Dehazing
papers.abstract: Dense haze reduces visibility and degrades camera-based perception, yet lightweight dehazing models often infer the severity of degradation solely from the hazy RGB image. Although the atmospheric scattering model provides a physically meaningful transmission prior, the best way to inject it into a compact network remains unclear. This paper compares three strategies within a fixed AOD-Net backbone: input concatenation, global feature-wise linear modulation, and the proposed Spatial Severity Modulation (SSM). SSM adds only 536 parameters and generates spatially varying feature adjustments from the full severity map. Across three seeds on Dense-Haze, input concatenation is competitive but more variable than the baseline, while global modulation shows high seed sensitivity. SSM with a severity-weighted $\mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{1}}$ loss achieves the highest and most stable PSNR, reaching 12.96±0.06 dB, compared with 12.53±0.14 dB for the baseline. SSIM remains comparable, while higher LPIPS indicates a pixel-fidelity-perceptual-similarity trade-off. A factorial ablation shows that the weighted loss is associated with more stable SSM training under the evaluated protocol. However, inference-time prior swapping changes PSNR by at most 0.07 dB, suggesting that Dense-Haze represents a boundary case with limited spatial prior information. The framework is relevant to traffic monitoring, surveillance, autonomous perception, and edge-based environmental imaging.
